from.place: Assertion (3): Roos comparison for a K-injective tower

title: Roos comparison on split-term complexes
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with countable products and let $J$ be an integer-indexed cochain complex of inverse systems [def-weil-inverse-system], with all transitions split epimorphisms in every degree. There exist a termwise product complex $P$, its transition chain map $s=1-\mathrm{shift}$ [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism], a termwise kernel complex $L$ with inclusion $i:L\to P$, and a complex $C$ identified in degree $p+1$ with $P^p\oplus P^{p+1}$. The product differential is componentwise that of $J$, and the differential on $C$ is $(y,x)\mapsto(-dy-sx,dx)$. There exists a quasi-isomorphism $\eta:L\to C$ with components $(0,i)$. The kernel inclusion is equipped with its termwise limiting kernel fork. This statement makes no K-injectivity assumption.

source.place: Tag 070M, split short exact sequence and cone comparison; original Roos node Steps 1,3,4

proof.text: Construct PJ with degree-p object the countable product of the terms of J.X p and differential Pi.map of the components of J.d. Product extensionality and d squared equals zero give a complex. The transition endomorphism commutes with this differential by towerTransitionEndomorphism_natural_backward and naturality of J.d, giving sJ.

In each degree choose sections of the split transition morphisms. On the product recursively define a_0=0 and a_(n+1)=(a_n-pr_n) composed with the n-th section. The section equation gives a_(n+1) composed with the transition equal to a_n-pr_n. Hence Pi.lift a composed with sJ is the identity, by its projections. Thus every component of sJ is an epimorphism.

Let LJ be kernel sJ, with its kernel inclusion. Apply the degreewise-epi kernel/shifted-cone theorem to obtain kappa: LJ to Cone(sJ)[-1], a quasi-isomorphism with the stated projection equations. Evaluation of complexes preserves kernels, so every component of the kernel inclusion is a limiting kernel fork.

Use CJ=Cone(sJ)[-1]. Compose the shift degree isomorphism and the cone biproduct isomorphism with the biproduct braiding. The two differential projection identities of Mathlib homotopyCofiber, together with the minus sign of the shift by -1, give exactly (-dy-sJ x,dx). Reindex the projection equations of kappa and compose with the braiding: its components become (0,iJ). The quasi-isomorphism is the kappa already supplied by the kernel/cone theorem.

lean.statement:
theorem roos_split_comparison
    (A : Type u) [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A]
    [HasLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) A]
    (J : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ℤ)
    (hSplit : ∀ (p : ℤ) (n : ℕ),
      IsSplitEpi ((J.X p).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op)) :
    ∃ (PJ LJ CJ : CochainComplex A ℤ)
      (ePJ : ∀ p : ℤ, PJ.X p ≅ ∏ᶜ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (J.X p).obj (Opposite.op n)))
      (sJ : PJ ⟶ PJ) (iJ : LJ ⟶ PJ)
      (hKJ : ∀ p : ℤ, iJ.f p ≫ sJ.f p = 0)
      (eCJ : ∀ p : ℤ, CJ.X (p + 1) ≅ PJ.X p ⊞ PJ.X (p + 1))
      (etaJ : LJ ⟶ CJ)
      (_hLJ : ∀ p : ℤ, IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι (iJ.f p) (hKJ p))),
      (∀ p q : ℤ, PJ.d p q ≫ (ePJ q).hom =
      (ePJ p).hom ≫ Limits.Pi.map (fun n ↦ (J.d p q).app (Opposite.op n))) ∧
      (∀ p : ℤ, sJ.f p = (ePJ p).hom ≫
      towerTransitionEndomorphism
        (fun n ↦ (J.X p).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) ≫ (ePJ p).inv) ∧
      (∀ p : ℤ, CJ.d (p + 1) (p + 1 + 1) ≫ (eCJ (p + 1)).hom =
      (eCJ p).hom ≫ biprod.lift
        (-(biprod.fst ≫ PJ.d p (p + 1)) - biprod.snd ≫ sJ.f (p + 1))
        (biprod.snd ≫ PJ.d (p + 1) (p + 1 + 1))) ∧
      (∀ p : ℤ, etaJ.f (p + 1) ≫ (eCJ p).hom = biprod.lift 0 (iJ.f (p + 1))) ∧
      QuasiIso etaJ
